Speaking in Abuja on Thursday, 19th November, 2026 at the National Grassroots Sports Development Summit 2026, convened under the theme “Creating a New Pathway for Sustainable Grassroots Sports Development in Nigeria,” Dikko outlined a comprehensive vision aimed at repositioning the sector for long-term success.
Tinubu Seeks Sports Integration Into Nigeria’s Educational Curriculum
At the core of his address was the assertion that a competitive sports industry requires an accessible ecosystem where talent is identified early.
“Our ambition must go beyond preparing athletes for competitions and winning medals,” Dikko stated. “We must create an environment where sports participation is accessible to all, talent is identified and nurtured early, and the wider sports ecosystem contributes meaningfully to national development.”
To achieve this, the Chairman highlighted the need for a deliberate focus on mass participation, school and community sports, sustainable infrastructure, and technical development. He also stressed the immense economic potential of the sector, noting that a structured pathway connecting grassroots participation to elite opportunities will drive employment, encourage entrepreneurship, and attract investment for young people.
Dikko noted, however, that government alone cannot achieve this vision. He called for a coordinated, multi-sectoral approach to sports development.
“While government has a critical role in providing policy direction, institutional support and an enabling environment, the private sector, state and local governments, sports federations, educational institutions, development partners and community organisations must all be active participants in this process,” he said.
Dikko commended the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development for convening the summit, as well as the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) for providing technical and policy support.
In closing, he urged participants to move beyond dialogue and focus on tangible outcomes.
“The true value of this Summit will ultimately be determined not by the conversations we hold, but by the commitments, partnerships and actions that follow,” Dikko charged the attendees, urging a collective commitment to building a system that strengthens communities and unlocks the full economic and social value of Nigerian sports.
